Content:
Given two vectors [MATH: \mathbf{a}_1] and [MATH: \mathbf{a}_2,] the set of all possible linear combinations of [MATH: \mathbf{a}_1] and [MATH: \mathbf{a}_2] is
[MATH: U = \left\{ x_1 \mathbf{a}_1 + x_2 \mathbf{a}_2 \: : \: x_1,x_2\in\mathbb{R} \right\}.]

Content:
The set [MATH: U] is also called the linear span of [MATH: \mathbf{a}_1] and [MATH: \mathbf{a}_2,] and is denoted by [MATH: \textrm{Span}\{ \mathbf{a}_1, \mathbf{a}_2 \}.] We say that [MATH: \mathbf{a}_1] and [MATH: \mathbf{a}_2] are the generators of [MATH: \textrm{Span}\{ \mathbf{a}_1, \mathbf{a}_2 \}.]

Content:
For example, let's find the linear span generated by the following vectors:
[MATH: [− 1; 1; 0]]

Content:
From the definition of linear span, we know that if [MATH: \mathbf{b} \in \textrm{Span}\{ \mathbf{a}_1, \mathbf{a}_2 \},] then [MATH: \mathbf{b}] must take the form
[MATH: \mathbf{b} = x_1\mathbf{a_1} + x_2\mathbf{a_2}]
for some [MATH: x_1,x_2\in\mathbb{R}.] So, we have

Content:
[MATH: b|= x_{1}a_{1} + x_{2}a_{2}; = x_{1}[− 1; 1; 0] + x_{2}[3; 2; − 1]; = [− x_{1}; x_{1}; 0] + [3x_{2}; 2x_{2}; − x_{2}]; = [− x_{1} + 3x_{2}; x_{1} + 2x_{2}; − x_{2}].]

Content:
Therefore the linear span of [MATH: \mathbf{a}_1] and [MATH: \mathbf{a}_2] is
[MATH: [− x_{1} + 3x_{2}; x_{1} + 2x_{2}; − x_{2}]]

Content:
Geometrically, [MATH: \textrm{Span}\{ \mathbf{a}_1, \mathbf{a}_2 \}] can be viewed as the plane [MATH: \Pi] that passes through the origin and is parallel to the vectors [MATH: \mathbf{a}_1] and [MATH: \mathbf{a}_2,] as shown below.

So, we have the following system of equations: [MATH: {x_{1} + 5x_{2} = 8; x_{1} + 3x_{2} = 2; 2x_{1} + 2x_{2} = − 5]

To solve the system above, we set up and row reduce an augmented matrix:

[MATH: ∼[1|5|8; 1|3|2; 2|2|− 5]|R_{2}|:=R_{2} − R_{1}; ∼[1|5|8; 0|− 2|− 6; 2|2|− 5]|R_{3}|:=R_{3} − 2R_{1}; ∼[1|5|8; 0|− 2|− 6; 0|− 8|− 21]|R_{2}|:= − (1)/(2)R_{2}; ∼[1|5|8; 0|1|3; 0|− 8|− 21]|R_{3}|:=R_{3} + 8R_{2}; ∼[1|5|8; 0|1|3; 0|0|3]|R_{2}|↔R_{3}]

The third row of the augmented matrix now corresponds to the equation [MATH: 0x_1 + 0x_2 = 3,] which has no solution.

So, there are no values of [MATH: x_1] and [MATH: x_2] such that [MATH: x_{1}a_{1} + x_{2}a_{2}|= b; x_{1}[1; 2; 1] + x_{2}[5; 2; 3]|= [8; − 5; 2].]

Therefore, we conclude that [MATH: \mathbf{b}] does not lie in [MATH: \textrm{Span}\{ \mathbf{a_1}, \mathbf{a_2} \}.]

sections.normalized_html: The linear span of vectors can be interpreted geometrically as the points in space that can be reached by adding multiples of those vectors.

lesson.readable_text:
Item 1 — Tutorial: Introduction

Content:
Given two vectors [MATH: \mathbf{a}_1] and [MATH: \mathbf{a}_2,] the set of all possible linear combinations of [MATH: \mathbf{a}_1] and [MATH: \mathbf{a}_2] is
[MATH: U = \left\{ x_1 \mathbf{a}_1 + x_2 \mathbf{a}_2 \: : \: x_1,x_2\in\mathbb{R} \right\}.]

Content:
The set [MATH: U] is also called the linear span of [MATH: \mathbf{a}_1] and [MATH: \mathbf{a}_2,] and is denoted by [MATH: \textrm{Span}\{ \mathbf{a}_1, \mathbf{a}_2 \}.] We say that [MATH: \mathbf{a}_1] and [MATH: \mathbf{a}_2] are the generators of [MATH: \textrm{Span}\{ \mathbf{a}_1, \mathbf{a}_2 \}.]

Content:
For example, let's find the linear span generated by the following vectors:
[MATH: [− 1; 1; 0]]

Content:
From the definition of linear span, we know that if [MATH: \mathbf{b} \in \textrm{Span}\{ \mathbf{a}_1, \mathbf{a}_2 \},] then [MATH: \mathbf{b}] must take the form
[MATH: \mathbf{b} = x_1\mathbf{a_1} + x_2\mathbf{a_2}]
for some [MATH: x_1,x_2\in\mathbb{R}.] So, we have

Content:
[MATH: b|= x_{1}a_{1} + x_{2}a_{2}; = x_{1}[− 1; 1; 0] + x_{2}[3; 2; − 1]; = [− x_{1}; x_{1}; 0] + [3x_{2}; 2x_{2}; − x_{2}]; = [− x_{1} + 3x_{2}; x_{1} + 2x_{2}; − x_{2}].]

Content:
Therefore the linear span of [MATH: \mathbf{a}_1] and [MATH: \mathbf{a}_2] is
[MATH: [− x_{1} + 3x_{2}; x_{1} + 2x_{2}; − x_{2}]]

Content:
Geometrically, [MATH: \textrm{Span}\{ \mathbf{a}_1, \mathbf{a}_2 \}] can be viewed as the plane [MATH: \Pi] that passes through the origin and is parallel to the vectors [MATH: \mathbf{a}_1] and [MATH: \mathbf{a}_2,] as shown below.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/d3f235df369da8fd14146c5c7f90942a]

---

Item 2 — Example: Determining Whether a Vector Lies in the Span of Given Vectors

Example Prompt:
Determine if [MATH: \mathbf{b}] lies in [MATH: \textrm{Span}\{ \mathbf{a_1}, \mathbf{a_2} \},] where
[MATH: [1; 1; 2]]

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
We know that [MATH: \mathbf{b} \in \textrm{Span}\{ \mathbf{a_1}, \mathbf{a_2} \}] if there exist [MATH: x_1] and [MATH: x_2] such that
[MATH: x_{1}a_{1} + x_{2}a_{2}|= b; x_{1}[1; 1; 2] + x_{2}[5; 3; 2]|= [8; 2; − 5].]

So, we have the following system of equations:
[MATH: {x_{1} + 5x_{2} = 8; x_{1} + 3x_{2} = 2; 2x_{1} + 2x_{2} = − 5]

To solve the system above, we set up and row reduce an augmented matrix:

[MATH: ∼[1|5|8; 1|3|2; 2|2|− 5]|R_{2}|:=R_{2} − R_{1}; ∼[1|5|8; 0|− 2|− 6; 2|2|− 5]|R_{3}|:=R_{3} − 2R_{1}; ∼[1|5|8; 0|− 2|− 6; 0|− 8|− 21]|R_{2}|:= − (1)/(2)R_{2}; ∼[1|5|8; 0|1|3; 0|− 8|− 21]|R_{3}|:=R_{3} + 8R_{2}; ∼[1|5|8; 0|1|3; 0|0|3]|R_{2}|↔R_{3}]

The third row of the augmented matrix now corresponds to the equation [MATH: 0x_1 + 0x_2 = 3,] which has no solution.

So, there are no values of [MATH: x_1] and [MATH: x_2] such that
[MATH: x_{1}a_{1} + x_{2}a_{2}|= b; x_{1}[1; 2; 1] + x_{2}[5; 2; 3]|= [8; − 5; 2].]

Therefore, we conclude that [MATH: \mathbf{b}] does not lie in [MATH: \textrm{Span}\{ \mathbf{a_1}, \mathbf{a_2} \}.]

We know that [MATH: \mathbf{b} \in \textrm{Span}\{ \mathbf{a_1}, \mathbf{a_2} \}] if there exist [MATH: x_1] and [MATH: x_2] such that

[MATH: x_{1}a_{1} + x_{2}a_{2}|= b; x_{1}[1; 5; 7] + x_{2}[− 2; 4; 2]|= [13; − 5; k].]

So, we have the following system of equations:
[MATH: {x_{1} − 2x_{2} = 13; 5x_{1} + 4x_{2} = − 5; 7x_{1} + 2x_{2} = k]

To solve the system above, we set up and row reduce an augmented matrix:

[MATH: ∼[1|− 2|13; 5|4|− 5; 7|2|k]|R_{2}|:=R_{2} − 5R_{1}; ∼[1|− 2|13; 0|14|− 70; 7|2|k]|R_{3}|:=R_{3} − 7R_{1}; ∼[1|− 2|13; 0|14|− 70; 0|16|k − 91]|R_{2}|:=(1)/(14)R_{2}; ∼[1|− 2|13; 0|1|− 5; 0|16|k − 91]|R_{3}|:=R_{3} − 16R_{2}; ∼[1|− 2|13; 0|1|− 5; 0|0|k − 11]]

The third row of the augmented matrix now corresponds to the equation [MATH: 0x_1 + 0x_2 = k-11]. Therefore, the system has a solution only if
[MATH: 0 = k-11 \quad \Rightarrow \quad k=11.]
